lesson.child_mission: Respectful debate states a side, listens to the other and rebuts ideas with reasons, never insults.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Turn "That’s stupid" into a rebuttal sentence about an idea.

FEEDBACK
Name the idea, give a counter-reason, keep the person respected.

CHECK
Winning by humiliation is not classroom debate.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Deliver a 60-second respectful debate turn with listen-back, rebut and calm close. Note one phrase that kept respect.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Respectful debate states a side, listens to the other and rebuts ideas with reasons, never insults.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Deliver a 60-second respectful debate turn with listen-back, rebut and calm close. Note one phrase that kept respect. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using debate on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Winning by humiliation is not classroom debate.. Correction: Name the idea, give a counter-reason, keep the person respected.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Winning by humiliation is not classroom debate. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating debate on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with debate, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about debate with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for debate. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.explain:
Respectful debate states a side, listens to the other and rebuts ideas with reasons, never insults.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
